transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Since my grandson was killed, I just… I can’t feel warmth or happiness anymore. My daughter can sit right beside me, hold my hand, and I know I love her, but inside I don’t feel it at all.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
I’m not sure I’d call it sad exactly. I just feel… empty, more than anything.
Did these feelings start after your grandson was killed?
Yes. It started when he was killed—six days ago, outside the community center.
Are you grieving your grandson?
I don’t know. I know he’s gone, and I know I loved him. But I don’t feel much of anything right now.
Do you feel depressed?
I don’t know if it’s depression. Since my grandson was killed, even when my daughter sits with me and holds my hand, I know I love her, but I can’t feel any warmth from it inside.
Since your grandson died, have you had any moment at all when you felt even a little warmth or comfort?
No. My daughter holds my hand, sits right beside me—I know I love her—but I can’t feel any warmth or comfort from it inside.
Since your grandson died, have you felt sad most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I just feel sort of empty most of the time.
Since your grandson died, have things you usually enjoy felt pleasurable at all?
No… not really. Even with my daughter beside me, holding my hand, I know I love her, but I just can’t feel any warmth or pleasure from it inside.
Since your grandson died, have you been feeling depressed?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I just feel empty, like there’s nothing much inside me.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?
No… I haven’t been thinking that I’d be better off dead.
Since your grandson died, have these feelings made it hard for you to do your usual daily activities?

Yes. I’ve stopped going to my walking club, and I can’t bring myself to help plan the funeral repast. Those are people and responsibilities my family usually depends on me for, but I just… can’t do it.
Since your grandson died, have you found yourself longing or yearning for him?
I’m not sure what you mean by longing. I just feel empty since he died.
Do these feelings seem stronger than what you would expect after your grandson’s death?
I don’t know. I mean, it feels very heavy, but I don’t know what I’m supposed to expect.
Since your grandson died, have you been feeling worthless?
I don’t think so. I feel very sad and empty, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless.
Since your grandson died, have you felt sad or down?
I’m not really sure how to separate that from everything else. I just feel empty and heavy most of the time.
Since your grandson died, have you found yourself wanting him back or reaching for him in your mind?
I’m not sure what you mean by reaching for him in my mind. I think about him, of course, but I don’t know if that’s what you’re asking.
Since your grandson died, have you found yourself strongly wanting him back?
I don’t know that I’d say strongly wanting him back. I miss him, but I’m not sure how to put it beyond that.
Since your grandson died, have you been feeling hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I just don’t know what I’m supposed to feel right now.
Since your grandson died, have you found yourself crying?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to whether I’ve been crying or not.
Since your grandson died, have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether my sleep has changed.
